styleAnswer.evidence: The toilet reads clearly as a white and grey porcelain prop with a small blue water accent. Its ramp is shallow, about 4 steps (white, light grey, mid grey, dark) against the references' 5-6, and it has little grain or per-surface speckle. Every dark edge pixel is neutral (100% near-neutral), so the outline is a uniform neutral dark line around the whole shape rather than a darker tone of the adjacent material. The hedge (0%), stall (1%) and well (33%) all use tinted edges instead. The 100% neutral share is shared only by the iron lamp, where a neutral outline suits the material. Visible tones per tile are 9, equal to the hedge but well below the stall (17) and well (20). There are no flat 5x5 fills, which is a point in its favour. Overall it looks more like a sticker than the references, with a thinner ramp and a neutral outline. When in doubt, fail.
